prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests with the same JSON-RPC request id overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). Both PRs add a check that rejects a request whose id is already in flight with a 400 Bad Request. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests with the same JSON-RPC request id overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). Both PRs add a check that rejects a request whose id is already in flight with a 400 Bad Request. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` on `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC ids that are distinct per spec (integer 1 vs string "1"), so it can wrongly 409 a fresh string id that matches an in-flight int id, and it doesn't guard against a request id equal to the `_GET_stream` sentinel key. #3221 replaces the naive stringification with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that avoids both the int/string collision and the GET_STREAM_KEY collision, while implementing the same duplicate-in-flight-id rejection as #3063. It's a strict superset fix for the same underlying race, so #3063 can be closed in favor of it.

prs.title: fix(oauth): avoid lock contention for long-running requests
prs.author: ctaylor86
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: `context.lock` in `async_auth_flow` is held across the entire request/response cycle (including the outgoing protected request and, for #2858/#3252, the refresh/auth-flow yields), serializing unrelated concurrent requests on a single provider and stalling long-running requests behind unrelated auth work. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: `context.lock` in `async_auth_flow` is held across the entire request/response cycle (including the outgoing protected request and, for #2858/#3252, the refresh/auth-flow yields), serializing unrelated concurrent requests on a single provider and stalling long-running requests behind unrelated auth work. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3243 achieves the same lock-scope narrowing as #2858 and the same 'release lock before the protected request is sent' restructuring as #3252, but also closes a task-affinity hazard both leave open: `anyio.Lock` must be released by the same task that acquired it, while httpx can resume or close an auth-flow generator on a different task at the refresh/authorization yield points that #2858 and #3252 still hold inside `context.lock`. #3243 switches to `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` and adds a separate `flow_lock` scoped to refresh/authorization transitions, so those yields are no longer exposed to the task-mismatch failure.

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe
prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (esp. UrlElicitationRequiredError) aren't pickle-safe: default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data) which doesn't match subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) -- raising TypeError on unpickle (issue #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (esp. UrlElicitationRequiredError) aren't pickle-safe: default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data) which doesn't match subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) -- raising TypeError on unpickle (issue #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Fixes __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(restored, *args), with the object's __dict__ passed as pickle state -- this restores every subclass's extra instance attributes (e.g. UrlElicitationRequiredError._elicitations) generically without calling any subclass constructor or classmethod. #2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, leaving other MCPError subclasses (e.g. NoBackChannelError) with the same unpickling bug unfixed. #2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes a type check (if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError: from_error(...) else from_error_data(...)), so it only works for subclasses whose from_error_data matches semantics and needs a special case per divergent subclass; #3262 needs no such dispatch. #3262's test diff also imports NoBackChannelError, indicating pickle coverage was extended beyond UrlElicitationRequiredError to verify the generic fix, which #2555's tests do not cover.

clusters.pick_reason: #3243 achieves the same lock-scope narrowing as #2858 and the same 'release lock before the protected request is sent' restructuring as #3252, but also closes a task-affinity hazard both leave open: `anyio.Lock` must be released by the same task that acquired it, while httpx can resume or close an auth-flow generator on a different task at the refresh/authorization yield points that #2858 and #3252 still hold inside `context.lock`. #3243 switches to `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` and adds a separate `flow_lock` scoped to refresh/authorization transitions, so those yields are no longer exposed to the task-mismatch failure.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` on `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC ids that are distinct per spec (integer 1 vs string "1"), so it can wrongly 409 a fresh string id that matches an in-flight int id, and it doesn't guard against a request id equal to the `_GET_stream` sentinel key. #3221 replaces the naive stringification with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that avoids both the int/string collision and the GET_STREAM_KEY collision, while implementing the same duplicate-in-flight-id rejection as #3063. It's a strict superset fix for the same underlying race, so #3063 can be closed in favor of it.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Concurrent requests with the same JSON-RPC request id overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). clusters.pick_reason: Fixes __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(restored, *args), with the object's __dict__ passed as pickle state -- this restores every subclass's extra instance attributes (e.g. UrlElicitationRequiredError._elicitations) generically without calling any subclass constructor or classmethod. #2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, leaving other MCPError subclasses (e.g. NoBackChannelError) with the same unpickling bug unfixed. #2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes a type check (if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError: from_error(...) else from_error_data(...)), so it only works for subclasses whose from_error_data matches semantics and needs a special case per divergent subclass; #3262 needs no such dispatch. #3262's test diff also imports NoBackChannelError, indicating pickle coverage was extended beyond UrlElicitationRequiredError to verify the generic fix, which #2555's tests do not cover.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs branch from the identical session.py base commit (243eef5ae6) and edit the same ~15-line block of RequestResponder.cancel() (lines 141-155), so only one can merge cleanly. #2493 simply deletes the error-response code with no replacement, so a locally-triggered cancellation (timeout or caller-initiated) leaves the peer with neither a response nor a notification. #2514 covers that same client-CancelledNotification case plus timeout and caller-cancellation triggers (per its title) by adding CancelledNotificationParams and having cancel() emit a spec-compliant notifications/cancelled, a strict superset of what #2493 fixes. Applying #2514 alone still leaves the stale explanatory comment/log line in server.py's _handle_request (currently only updated by #2493) to be reconciled.

clusters.pick_reason: #3243 achieves the same lock-scope narrowing as #2858 and the same 'release lock before the protected request is sent' restructuring as #3252, but also closes a task-affinity hazard both leave open: `anyio.Lock` must be released by the same task that acquired it, while httpx can resume or close an auth-flow generator on a different task at the refresh/authorization yield points that #2858 and #3252 still hold inside `context.lock`. #3243 switches to `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` and adds a separate `flow_lock` scoped to refresh/authorization transitions, so those yields are no longer exposed to the task-mismatch failure.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` on `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC ids that are distinct per spec (integer 1 vs string "1"), so it can wrongly 409 a fresh string id that matches an in-flight int id, and it doesn't guard against a request id equal to the `_GET_stream` sentinel key. #3221 replaces the naive stringification with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that avoids both the int/string collision and the GET_STREAM_KEY collision, while implementing the same duplicate-in-flight-id rejection as #3063. It's a strict superset fix for the same underlying race, so #3063 can be closed in favor of it.
